key_insight: The paper replaces global score estimation with a local Fokker–Planck heat-ball averaging framework that gives exact mean-value representations for score and related quantities in nonlinear diffusions.
engineering_relevance: This could improve score-based generative modeling and Langevin sampling in high dimensions by reducing error in low-density regions where accurate scores matter most.
method: Time-change the Fokker–Planck equation into a standard inhomogeneous heat equation and derive local heat-ball mean-value formulas for score, density, log-density, and entropy density.
Introduce a κ-measure with an exact factorized Monte Carlo sampler, giving unit per-sample weight and χ²₂ radial concentration.
Show the small-radius limit recovers the pointwise Fokker–Planck residual, linking the method to existing global FP-residual and DSM objectives.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation on 2D structured data, 256-dimensional MNIST, and a sampler study confirming the claimed concentration laws.
watch_item: Practical use may depend on the explicit dimension-dependent drift budget and the cost/variance behavior of heat-ball Monte Carlo in very high dimensions.
paper_title: Local Fokker--Planck Geometry for Score Estimation: Heat-Ball Mean-Value Representations and Exact High-Dimensional Sampling
